newsitem.title: PERU: Japan's ambassador apologizes for Peru rebel siege.
newsitem.headline: Japan's ambassador apologizes for Peru rebel siege.

text.p: Captive Japanese Ambassador Morihisa Aoki, the host of the ill-fated cocktail party stormed two weeks ago by Peruvian rebels, apologised on Tuesday for the embassy's involvement in the crisis.
"A thousand apologies from my government," he said in faltering Spanish.

Speaking in Japanese to journalists invited into his residence, where he was held along with 82 other hostages by the Marxist rebels, a tired- and solemn-looking Aoki also apologised to his own country.
"We deeply apologise to the (Japanese) government and the people for this involvement in this crisis," the ambassador said.

The Japanese embassy and Peruvian government have been criticised for lax security at the residence, which the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels have said was surprisingly easy to attack.

Two weeks ago the guerrillas took over 500 international high-ranking officials hostage and on Tuesday still held top Peruvian officials, foreign ambassadors and Japanese businessmen. They allowed groups of journalists into the building on Tuesday for the first time since the crisis began Dec. 17.

Aoki was presented to the media along with Masami Kobayashi, representative in Peru for the Japanese firm, Mitsui, Peru's Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela and government party congressman Gilberto Siura.

Aoki who hoped for "a peaceful solution and a release of all of us as soon as possible" said all of the remaining hostages -- including the 20-odd Japanese still held inside -- were calm, healthy and "maintained a sense of solidarity".
In the days following the siege, the Japanese ambassador has spoken only once before to the media.
On that occasion he made a joke on live radio, wryly asking forgiveness for the "unexpected length" of the lavish reception he held in honour of the Japanese empereror Akihito.
According to hostages released during the crisis, Aoki was keen to keep the captives in good spirits. They said his favourite quip was: "It has been a long but unforgettable party."
